results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $T_c(z) = z^2 + c$ for $c \in \mathbb{C}$ and let $T_c^n$ be its $n$-fold iterate. The Mandelbrot set $M$ is the set of $c \in \mathbb{C}$ for which the orbit of $0$ under $T_c$ is bounded: there is a real $R$ such that $|T_c^n(0)| \le R$ for every $n \ge 0$.

results.title: Fatou–Julia dichotomy for quadratic polynomials

Distinct edges may have the same endpoints (parallel edges), and the two endpoints of an edge may coincide (a loop). Neither $V$ nor $E$ is required to be finite.

results.title: Finite multigraphs with at least one edge
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A multigraph $G$ is finite and nontrivial when its set of vertices and its set of edges are both finite and it has at least one edge. These are the graphs on which the cycle-continuous order is considered.

results.title: Binary cycle space
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $G$ be a multigraph. A set $S$ of edges of $G$ is a binary cycle when $S$ is finite and every vertex $v$ is an endpoint of an even number of edges of $S$, where only edges with exactly one endpoint equal to $v$ are counted; loops are not counted, which agrees modulo $2$ with counting each loop twice. The cycle space of $G$ is the set of all binary cycles of $G$.

results.title: Cycle-continuous maps
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $G$ and $H$ be multigraphs. A map $f$ from the edges of $G$ to the edges of $H$ is cycle-continuous when, for every binary cycle $C$ of $H$, the preimage $f^{-1}(C)$ is a binary cycle of $G$.

results.title: Infinite antichains in the cycle-continuous order
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: There is a sequence $G_0, G_1, G_2, \dots$ of pairwise distinct finite multigraphs, each with at least one edge, such that for all $i \ne j$ there is no cycle-continuous map from the edges of $G_i$ to the edges of $G_j$.

results.title: Samal's theorem: infinite antichains in the cycle-continuous order exist
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: There is a sequence $G_0, G_1, G_2, \dots$ of pairwise distinct finite multigraphs, each with at least one edge, such that for all $i \ne j$ there is no cycle-continuous map from the edges of $G_i$ to the edges of $G_j$.

results.title: Probability that two genes differ at a biallelic site
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The probability `a (1 - b) + b (1 - a)` that a gene from a population with allele frequency `a` and a gene from a population with allele frequency `b` differ at a biallelic site.

results.title: Squared frequency difference via pairwise heterozygosity
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: `(a - b) ^ 2 = hetPair a b - (hetPair a a + hetPair b b) / 2`.

results.title: Expected heterozygosity between populations
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The expected heterozygosity `π X Y = 𝔼[hetPair (p X) (p Y)]` between populations `X` and `Y` (within population `X` when `Y = X`).

results.title: Integrability of pairwise heterozygosity
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: `hetPair` of square-integrable frequencies is integrable on a finite measure space.

results.title: Peter's formula for $f_2$ via expected heterozygosity
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Peter (2016): `f2 A B = π A B - (π A A + π B B) / 2`.

results.title: Column mean of a genotype matrix
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The column mean `(1 / n) ∑ i, Z i s` of locus `s` over the `n` samples.

results.title: Column-centred genotype matrix
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The genotype matrix with columns centred over the samples.

results.title: Sample covariance of the centred genotype matrix
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The sample covariance `C i j = (1 / L) ∑ s, X i s * X j s` of the centred genotype matrix `X` over the `L` loci.

results.title: Number of pairwise differences between samples
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The number of pairwise differences `d i j = ∑ s, (Z i s - Z j s) ^ 2` (for `0`/`1` haplotypes, the number of loci at which samples `i` and `j` differ).

results.title: Double centring of a square matrix
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The double centring `t̄ i· + t̄ ·j - t i j - t̄ ··` of a square matrix `t` (row, column and grand means over the `n` indices).

results.title: Genotype covariance as double-centred pairwise differences
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: McVean (2009), deterministic form: the covariance of the centred genotype matrix is the double centring of the pairwise-difference matrix, divided by `2 L`.

results.caption: Theorem
